explain_task.question: In the revised model, explain exactly why `recovery_Genoa = 1` can be optimal while `adriatic_pool = 0`, and trace that logic across the code, the CSV fields, and the business brief. Your answer must name the code variables `short[p]`, `rec[p]`, `pool`, and at least one shipment variable such as `x[w][p]`/`ship_w_p`; cite the exact CSV columns and parameter values that make Genoa’s local desk activate but keep the Adriatic pooled desk closed; and identify which revised objective terms and new constraints caused the objective to fall from 904590.0 to 749100.0 relative to the original `x[(i,j)]` transportation model in `src/formulation.tex`. Also interpret the LP-relaxation state (`recovery_Genoa = 0.9`, `recovery_Venice = 0.266666...`, `adriatic_pool` reduced cost 25000.0): which constraints are effectively binding, what is the business meaning of those marginal values/slacks, and why would a linear shadow-price extrapolation fail once shortage crosses a grace band or the Adriatic trigger?
